papers.title: MoManipVLA: Transferring Vision-language-action Models for General Mobile Manipulation
papers.abstract: Mobile manipulation is the fundamental challenge for robotics to assist humans with diverse tasks and environments in everyday life. However, conventional mobile manipulation approaches often struggle to generalize across different tasks and environments because of the lack of large-scale training.In contrast, recent advances in vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown impressive generalization capabilities, but these foundation models are developed for fixed-base manipulation tasks.Therefore, we propose an efficient policy adaptation framework to transfer pre-trained VLA models of fix-base manipulation to mobile manipulation, so that high generalization ability across tasks and environments can be achieved in mobile manipulation policy.Specifically, we utilize pre-trained VLA models to generate waypoints of the end-effector with high generalization ability. We design motion planning objectives for the mobile base and the robot arm, which aim at maximizing the physical feasibility of the trajectory. Finally, we present an efficient bi-level objective optimization framework for trajectory generation, where the upper-level optimization predicts waypoints for base movement to enhance the manipulator policy space, and the lower-level optimization selects the optimal end-effector trajectory to complete the manipulation task. Extensive experimental results on OVMM and the real world demonstrate that our method achieves a 4.2% higher success rate than the state-of-the-art mobile manipulation, and only requires 50 training cost for real world deployment due to the strong generalization ability in the pre-trained VLA models.

papers.title: TASTE-Rob: Advancing Video Generation of Task-Oriented Hand-Object Interaction for Generalizable Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: We address key limitations in existing datasets and models for task-oriented hand-object interaction video generation, a critical approach of generating video demonstrations for robotic imitation learning. Current datasets, such as Ego4D, often suffer from inconsistent view perspectives and misaligned interactions, leading to reduced video quality and limiting their applicability for precise imitation learning tasks. Towards this end, we introduce TASTE-Rob -- a pioneering large-scale dataset of 100,856 ego-centric hand-object interaction videos. Each video is meticulously aligned with language instructions and recorded from a consistent camera viewpoint to ensure interaction clarity. By fine-tuning a Video Diffusion Model (VDM) on TASTE-Rob, we achieve realistic object interactions, though we observed occasional inconsistencies in hand grasping postures. To enhance realism, we introduce a three-stage pose-refinement pipeline that improves hand posture accuracy in generated videos. Our curated dataset, coupled with the specialized pose-refinement framework, provides notable performance gains in generating high-quality, task-oriented hand-object interaction videos, resulting in achieving superior generalizable robotic manipulation. To foster further advancements in the field, TASTE-Rob dataset and source code will be made publicly available on our website https://taste-rob.github.io.

papers.title: Prior Does Matter: Visual Navigation via Denoising Diffusion Bridge Models
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in diffusion-based imitation learning, which shows impressive performance in modeling multimodal distributions and training stability, have led to substantial progress in various robot learning tasks. In visual navigation, previous diffusion-based policies typically generate action sequences by initiating from denoising Gaussian noise. However, the target action distribution often diverges significantly from Gaussian noise, leading to redundant denoising steps and increased learning complexity. Additionally, the sparsity of effective action distributions makes it challenging for the policy to generate accurate actions without guidance. To address these issues, we propose a novel, unified visual navigation framework leveraging the denoising diffusion bridge models named NaviBridger. This approach enables action generation by initiating from any informative prior actions, enhancing guidance and efficiency in the denoising process. We explore how diffusion bridges can enhance imitation learning in visual navigation tasks and further examine three source policies for generating prior actions. Extensive experiments in both simulated and real-world indoor and outdoor scenarios demonstrate that NaviBridger accelerates policy inference and outperforms the baselines in generating target action sequences. Code is available at https://github.com/hren20/NaiviBridger.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Cross-View Correspondence with Predictive Cycle Consistency
papers.abstract: Learning self-supervised visual correspondence is a long-studied task fundamental to visual understanding and human perception. However, existing correspondence methods largely focus on small image transformations, such as object tracking in high-framerate videos or learning pixel-to-pixel mappings between images with high view overlap. This severely limits their application in dynamic multi-view settings such as robot imitation learning. In this work, we introduce Predictive Cycle Consistency for learning object correspondence between extremely disjoint views of a scene without paired segmentation data. Our technique bootstraps object correspondence pseudolabels from raw image segmentations using conditional grayscale colorization and a cycle-consistency refinement prior. We then train deep ViTs on these pseudolabels, which we use to generate higher-quality pseudolabels and iteratively train better correspondence models. We demonstrate the performance of our method under both extreme in-the-wild camera view changes and across large temporal gaps in video. Our approach beats all prior supervised and prior SoTA self-supervised correspondence models on the EgoExo4D correspondence benchmark (+6.7 IoU Exo Query) and the prior SoTA self-supervised methods SiamMAE and DINO V1&V2 on the DAVIS-2017 and LVOS datasets across large frame gaps.

papers.title: MobileH2R: Learning Generalizable Human to Mobile Robot Handover Exclusively from Scalable and Diverse Synthetic Data
papers.abstract: This paper introduces MobileH2R, a framework for learning generalizable vision-based human-to-mobile-robot (H2MR) handover skills. Unlike traditional fixed-base handovers, this task requires a mobile robot to reliably receive objects in a large workspace enabled by its mobility. Our key insight is that generalizable handover skills can be developed in simulators using high-quality synthetic data, without the need for real-world demonstrations. To achieve this, we propose a scalable pipeline for generating diverse synthetic full-body human motion data, an automated method for creating safe and imitation-friendly demonstrations, and an efficient 4D imitation learning method for distilling large-scale demonstrations into closed-loop policies with base-arm coordination. Experimental evaluations in both simulators and the real world show significant improvements (at least +15% success rate) over baseline methods in all cases. Experiments also validate that large-scale and diverse synthetic data greatly enhances robot learning, highlighting our scalable framework.

papers.title: Spatial-Temporal Graph Diffusion Policy with Kinematic Modeling for Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Despite the significant success of imitation learning in robotic manipulation, its application to bimanual tasks remains highly challenging. Existing approaches mainly learn a policy to predict a distant next-best end-effector pose (NBP) and then compute the corresponding joint rotation angles for motion using inverse kinematics. However, they suffer from two important issues: (1) rarely considering the physical robotic structure , which may cause self-collisions or interferences, and (2) overlooking the kinematics constraint , which may result in the predicted poses not conforming to the actual limitations of the robot joints. In this paper, we propose Kinematics enhanced Spatial-TemporAl gRaph Diffuser (KStar Diffuser). Specifically, (1)to incorporate the physical robot structure information into action prediction, KStar Diffuser maintains a dynamic spatial-temporal graph according to the physical bimanual joint motions at continuous timesteps. This dynamic graph serves as the robot-structure condition for denoising the actions; (2) to make the NBP learning objective consistent with kinematics, we introduce the differentiable kinematics to provide the reference for optimizing KStar Diffuser. This module regularizes the policy to predict more reliable and kinematics-aware next end-effector poses. Experimental results show that our method effectively leverages the physical structural information and generates kinematics-aware actions in both simulation and real-world.

papers.title: G3Flow: Generative 3D Semantic Flow for Pose-aware and Generalizable Object Manipulation
papers.abstract: Recent advances in imitation learning for 3D robotic manipulation have shown promising results with diffusion-based policies. However, achieving human-level dexterity requires seamless integration of geometric precision and semantic understanding. We present G3Flow, a novel framework that constructs real-time semantic flow, a dynamic, object-centric 3D semantic representation by leveraging foundation models. Our approach uniquely combines 3D generative models for digital twin creation, vision foundation models for semantic feature extraction, and robust pose tracking for continuous semantic flow updates. This integration enables complete semantic understanding even under occlusions while eliminating manual annotation requirements. By incorporating semantic flow into diffusion policies, we demonstrate significant improvements in both terminal-constrained manipulation and cross-object generalization. Extensive experiments across five simulation tasks show that G3Flow consistently outperforms existing approaches, achieving up to 68.3% and 50.1% average success rates on terminal-constrained manipulation and cross-object generalization tasks respectively. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of G3Flow in enhancing real-time dynamic semantic feature understanding for robotic manipulation policies.

papers.title: SkillMimic: Learning Basketball Interaction Skills from Demonstrations
papers.abstract: Traditional reinforcement learning methods for human-object interaction (HOI) rely on labor-intensive, manually designed skill rewards that do not generalize well across different interactions. We introduce SkillMimic, a unified data-driven framework that fundamentally changes how agents learn interaction skills by eliminating the need for skill-specific rewards. Our key insight is that a unified HOI imitation reward can effectively capture the essence of diverse interaction patterns from HOI datasets. This enables SkillMimic to learn a single policy that not only masters multiple interaction skills but also facilitates skill transitions, with both diversity and generalization improving as the HOI dataset grows. For evaluation, we collect and introduce two basketball datasets containing approximately 35 minutes of diverse basketball skills. Extensive experiments show that SkillMimic successfully masters a wide range of basketball skills including stylistic variations in dribbling, layup, and shooting. Moreover, these learned skills can be effectively composed by a high-level controller to accomplish complex and long-horizon tasks such as consecutive scoring, opening new possibilities for scalable and generalizable interaction skill learning. Project page: https://ingrid789.github.io/SkillMimic/

papers.title: ManipTrans: Efficient Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation Transfer via Residual Learning
papers.abstract: Human hands play a central role in interacting, motivating increasing research in dexterous robotic manipulation. Data-driven embodied AI algorithms demand precise, large-scale, human-like manipulation sequences, which are challenging to obtain with conventional reinforcement learning or real-world teleoperation. To address this, we introduce ManipTrans, a novel two-stage method for efficiently transferring human bimanual skills to dexterous robotic hands in simulation. ManipTrans first pre-trains a generalist trajectory imitator to mimic hand motion, then fine-tunes a specific residual module under interaction constraints, enabling efficient learning and accurate execution of complex bimanual tasks. Experiments show that ManipTrans surpasses state-of-the-art methods in success rate, fidelity, and efficiency. Leveraging ManipTrans, we transfer multiple hand-object datasets to robotic hands, creating DexManipNet, a large-scale dataset featuring previously unexplored tasks like pen capping and bottle unscrewing. DexManipNet comprises 3.3K episodes of robotic manipulation and is easily extensible, facilitating further policy training for dexterous hands and enabling real-world deployments.

papers.title: VidBot: Learning Generalizable 3D Actions from In-the-Wild 2D Human Videos for Zero-Shot Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Future robots are envisioned as versatile systems capable of performing a variety of household tasks. The big question remains, how can we bridge the embodiment gap while minimizing physical robot learning, which fundamentally does not scale well. We argue that learning from in-the-wild human videos offers a promising solution for robotic manipulation tasks, as vast amounts of relevant data already exist on the internet. In this work, we present VidBot, a framework enabling zero-shot robotic manipulation using learned 3D affordance from in-the-wild monocular RGB-only human videos. VidBot leverages a pipeline to extract explicit representations from them, namely 3D hand trajectories from videos, combining a depth foundation model with structure-from-motion techniques to reconstruct temporally consistent, metric-scale 3D affordance representations agnostic to embodiments. We introduce a coarse-to-fine affordance learning model that first identifies coarse actions from the pixel space and then generates fine-grained interaction trajectories with a diffusion model, conditioned on coarse actions and guided by test-time constraints for context-aware interaction planning, enabling substantial generalization to novel scenes and embodiments. Extensive experiments demonstrate the efficacy of VidBot, which significantly outperforms counterparts across 13 manipulation tasks in zero-shot settings and can be seamlessly deployed across robot systems in real-world environments. VidBot paves the way for leveraging everyday human videos to make robot learning more scalable.

papers.title: OmniManip: Towards General Robotic Manipulation via Object-Centric Interaction Primitives as Spatial Constraints
papers.abstract: The development of general robotic systems capable of manipulating in unstructured environments is a significant challenge. While Vision-Language Models(VLM) excel in high-level commonsense reasoning, they lack the fine-grained 3D spatial understanding required for precise manipulation tasks. Fine-tuning VLM on robotic datasets to create Vision-Language-Action Models(VLA) is a potential solution, but it is hindered by high data collection costs and generalization issues. To address these challenges, we propose a novel object-centric representation that bridges the gap between VLM's high-level reasoning and the low-level precision required for manipulation. Our key insight is that an object's canonical space, defined by its functional affordances, provides a structured and semantically meaningful way to describe interaction primitives, such as points and directions. These primitives act as a bridge, translating VLM's commonsense reasoning into actionable 3D spatial constraints. In this context, we introduce a dual closed-loop, open-vocabulary robotic manipulation system: one loop for high-level planning through primitive resampling, interaction rendering and VLM checking, and another for low-level execution via 6D pose tracking. This design ensures robust, real-time control without requiring VLM fine-tuning. Extensive experiments demonstrate strong zero-shot generalization across diverse robotic manipulation tasks, highlighting the potential of this approach for automating large-scale data generation.

papers.title: DynScene: Scalable Generation of Dynamic Robotic Manipulation Scenes for Embodied AI
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation in embodied AI critically depends on large-scale, high-quality datasets that reflect realistic object interactions and physical dynamics. However, existing data collection pipelines are often slow, expensive, and heavily reliant on manual efforts. We present DynScene, a diffusion-based framework for generating dynamic robotic manipulation scenes directly from textual instructions. Unlike prior methods that focus solely on static environments or isolated robot actions, DynScene decomposes the generation into two phases static scene synthesis and action trajectory generation allowing fine-grained control and diversity. Our model enhances realism and physical feasibility through scene refinement (layout sampling, quaternion quantization) and leverages residual action representation to enable action augmentation, generating multiple diverse trajectories from a single static configuration. Experiments show DynScene achieves 26.8x faster generation, 1.84x higher accuracy, and 28% greater action diversity than human-crafted data. Furthermore, agents trained with DynScene exhibit up to 19.4% higher success rates across complex manipulation tasks. Our approach paves the way for scalable, automated dataset generation in robot learning.

papers.title: RoboGround: Robotic Manipulation with Grounded Vision-Language Priors
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in robotic manipulation have highlighted the potential of intermediate representations for improving policy generalization. In this work, we explore grounding masks as an effective intermediate representation, balancing two key advantages: (1) effective spatial guidance that specifies target objects and placement areas while also conveying information about object shape and size, and (2) broad generalization potential driven by large-scale vision-language models pretrained on diverse grounding datasets. We introduce \method, a grounding-aware robotic manipulation policy that leverages grounding masks as an intermediate representation to guide policy networks in object manipulation tasks. To further explore and enhance generalization, we propose an automated pipeline for generating large-scale, simulated data with a diverse set of objects and instructions. Extensive experiments show the value of our dataset and the effectiveness of grounding masks as intermediate guidance, significantly enhancing the generalization abilities of robot policies.

papers.title: PDFactor: Learning Tri-Perspective View Policy Diffusion Field for Multi-Task Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation based on visual observations and natural language instructions is a long-standing challenge in robotics. Yet prevailing approaches model action distribution by adopting explicit or implicit representations, which often struggle to achieve a trade-off between accuracy and efficiency. In response, we propose PDFactor, a novel framework that models action distribution with a hybrid triplane representation. In particular, PDFactor decomposes 3D point cloud into three orthogonal feature planes and leverages a tri-perspective view transformer to produce dense cubic features as a latent diffusion field aligned with observation space representing 6-DoF action probability distribution at an arbitrary location. We employ a small denoising network conceptually as both a parameterized loss function measuring the quality of the learned latent features and an action gradient decoder to sample actions from the latent diffusion field during inference. This design enables our PDFactor to benefit from spatial awareness of explicit representation and arbitrary resolution of implicit representation, rendering it with manipulation accuracy, inference efficiency, and model scalability. Experiments demonstrate that PDFactor outperforms state-of-the-art approaches across a diverse range of manipulation tasks in RLBench simulation. Moreover, PDFactor can effectively learn multi-task policies from a limited number of human demonstrations, achieving promising accuracy in a variety of real-world manipulation tasks.

papers.title: FlowRAM: Grounding Flow Matching Policy with Region-Aware Mamba Framework for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation in high-precision tasks is essential for numerous industrial and real-world applications where accuracy and speed are required. Yet current diffusion-based policy learning methods generally suffer from low computational efficiency due to the iterative denoising process during inference. Moreover, these methods do not fully explore the potential of generative models for enhancing information exploration in 3D environments. In response, we propose FlowRAM, a novel framework that leverages generative models to achieve region-aware perception, enabling efficient multimodal information processing. Specifically, we devise a Dynamic Radius Schedule, which enables adaptive perception, facilitating transitions from global scene comprehension to fine-grained geometric details. Furthermore, we integrate state space models to integrate multimodal information, while preserving linear computational complexity. In addition, we employ conditional flow matching to learn action poses by regressing deterministic vector fields, which simplifies the learning process while maintaining performance. We verify the effectiveness of the FlowRAM in the RLBench, an established manipulation benchmark, and achieve state-of-the-art performance. The results demonstrate that FlowRAM achieves a remarkable improvement, particularly in high-precision tasks, where it outperforms previous methods by 12.0% in average success rate. Additionally, FlowRAM is able to generate physically plausible actions for a variety of real-world tasks in less than 4 time steps, significantly increasing inference speed.

papers.title: RoboBrain: A Unified Brain Model for Robotic Manipulation from Abstract to Concrete
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown remarkable capabilities across various multimodal contexts. However, their application in robotic scenarios, particularly for long-horizon manipulation tasks, reveals significant limitations. These limitations arise from the current MLLMs lacking three essential robotic brain capabilities: Planning Capability, which involves decomposing complex manipulation instructions into manageable sub-tasks; Affordance Perception, the ability to recognize and interpret the affordances of interactive objects; and Trajectory Prediction, the foresight to anticipate the complete manipulation trajectory necessary for successful execution. To enhance the robotic brain's core capabilities from abstract to concrete, we introduce ShareRobot, a high-quality heterogeneous dataset that labels multi-dimensional information such as task planning, object affordance, and end-effector trajectory. ShareRobot's diversity and accuracy have been meticulously refined by three human annotators. Building on this dataset, we developed RoboBrain, an MLLM-based model that combines robotic and general multi-modal data, utilizes a multi-stage training strategy, and incorporates long videos and high-resolution images to improve its robotic manipulation capabilities.Extensive experiments demonstrate that RoboBrain achieves state-of-the-art performance across various obotic tasks, highlighting its potential to advance robotic brain capabilities.

papers.title: Object-Centric Prompt-Driven Vision-Language-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: In robotic manipulation, task goals can be conveyed through various modalities, such as language, goal images, and goal videos. However, natural language can be ambiguous, while images or videos may offer overly detailed specifications. To address these challenges, we propose a novel approach using comprehensive multi-modal prompts that explicitly convey both low-level actions and high-level planning in a simple manner. Specifically, for each key-frame in the task sequence, our method allows for manual or automatic generation of simple and expressive 2D visual prompts overlaid on RGB images. These prompts represent the required task goals, such as the end-effector pose and the desired movement direction after contact. We develop a training strategy that enables the model to interpret these visual-language prompts and predict the corresponding contact poses and movement directions in SE(3) space. Furthermore, by sequentially executing all key-frame steps, the model can complete long-horizon tasks. This approach not only helps the model explicitly understand the task objectives but also enhances its robustness on unseen tasks by providing easily interpretable prompts. We evaluate our method in both simulated and real-world environments, demonstrating its robust manipulation capabilities.

papers.title: Mitigating the Human-Robot Domain Discrepancy in Visual Pre-training for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Learning generalizable visual representations across different embodied environments is essential for effective robotic manipulation in real-world scenarios. However, the limited scale and diversity of robot demonstration data pose a significant challenge. Recent research has explored leveraging large-scale human activity data for pre-training, but the substantial morphological differences between humans and robots introduce a significant human-robot domain discrepancy, hindering the generalization of these models to downstream manipulation tasks. To overcome this, we propose a novel adaptation paradigm that leverages readily available paired human-robot video data to bridge the domain gap. Our method employs a human-robot contrastive alignment loss to align the semantics of human and robot videos, adapting pre-trained models to the robot domain in a parameter-efficient manner. Experiments on 20 simulated tasks across two different benchmarks and five real-world tasks demonstrate significant improvements. These results span both single-task and language-conditioned multi-task settings, evaluated using two different pre-trained models. Compared to existing pre-trained models, our adaptation method improves the average success rate by over 7% across multiple tasks on both simulated benchmarks and real-world evaluations.

papers.title: Think Small, Act Big: Primitive Prompt Learning for Lifelong Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Learning a generalist robot that can effectively leverage prior knowledge for continuous skill acquisition remains significantly challenging. Despite the success of experience replay and parameter-efficient methods in maintaining knowledge across skills, naively applying these methods causes a failure to leverage the shared primitives between skills. To tackle these issues, we propose Primitive Prompt Learning (PPL), to achieve lifelong robot manipulation via reusable and extensible primitives. Within our two stage learning scheme, we first learn a set of primitive prompts to model primitives through multi-skills pre-training stage, where motion-aware prompts are learned to capture semantic and motion shared primitives across different skills. Secondly, when acquiring new skills in lifelong span, new prompts are concatenated and optimized with frozen pretrained prompts, boosting the learning via knowledge transfer from old skills to new ones. For evaluation, we construct a large-scale skill dataset and conduct extensive experiments in both simulation and real-world tasks, demonstrating PPL's superior performance over state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: 3D-MVP: 3D Multiview Pretraining for Manipulation
papers.abstract: Recent works have shown that visual pretraining on egocentric datasets using masked autoencoders (MAE) can improve generalization for downstream robotics tasks. However, these approaches pretrain only on 2D images, while many robotics applications require 3D scene understanding. In this work, we propose 3D-MVP, a novel approach for 3D Multi-View Pretraining using masked autoencoders. We leverage Robotic View Transformer (RVT), which uses a multi-view transformer to understand the 3D scene and predict gripper pose actions. We split RVT's multi-view transformer into visual encoder and action decoder, and pretrain its visual encoder using masked autoencoding on large-scale 3D datasets such as Objaverse. We evaluate 3D-MVP on a suite of virtual robot manipulation tasks and demonstrate improved performance over baselines. Our results suggest that 3D-aware pretraining is a promising approach to improve generalization of vision-based robotic manipulation policies.

papers.title: Magma: A Foundation Model for Multimodal AI Agents
papers.abstract: We present Magma, a foundation model that serves multimodal AI agentic tasks in both the digital and physical worlds. Magma is a significant extension of vision-language (VL) models in that it not only retains the VL understanding ability (verbal intelligence) of the latter, but is also equipped with the ability to ground and act in the visual-spatial world (spatial-temporal intelligence). To endow agentic capabilities for tasks ranging from UI navigation to robot manipulation, Magma is trained on large amounts of heterogeneous datasets that span from images, videos to robotics data, where actionable visual objects (e.g. clickable buttons in GUI) in images are labeled by Set-of-Mark (SoM) for action grounding, and object movements (e.g. trace of human hands or robotic arms) in videos are labeled by Trace-of-Mark (ToM) for action planning. Extensive experiments show that SoM and ToM help bridge the gap between verbal and action abilities and significantly enhance spatio-temporal intelligence which is fundamental to agentic tasks, as shown in Fig.1. In particular, Magma creates new state-of-the-art results on UI navigation and robotic manipulation tasks, outperforming previous models that are specifically tailored to these tasks. Moreover, Magma preserves strong multimodal understanding ability and compares favorably to popular large multimodal models that are trained on much larger datasets. We have made our model and code public for reproducibility at https://microsoft.github.io/Magma.

papers.title: GENMANIP: LLM-driven Simulation for Generalizable Instruction-Following Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation in real-world settings remains challenging, especially regarding robust generalization. Existing simulation platforms lack sufficient support for exploring how policies adapt to varied instructions and scenarios. Thus, they lag behind the growing interest in instruction-following foundation models like LLMs, whose adaptability is crucial yet remains underexplored in fair comparisons. To bridge this gap, we introduce GenManip, a realistic tabletop simulation platform tailored for policy generalization studies. It features an automatic pipeline via LLM-driven task-oriented scene graph to synthesize large-scale, diverse tasks using 10K annotated 3D object assets. To systematically assess generalization, we present GenManip-Bench, a benchmark of 200 scenarios refined via human-in-the-loop corrections. We evaluate two policy types: (1) modular manipulation systems integrating foundation models for perception, reasoning, and planning, and (2) end-to-end policies trained through scalable data collection. Results show that while data scaling benefits end-to-end methods, modular systems enhanced with foundation models generalize more effectively across diverse scenarios. We anticipate this platform to facilitate critical insights for advancing policy generalization in realistic conditions. All code will be made publicly available.

papers.title: Lift3D Policy: Lifting 2D Foundation Models for Robust 3D Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: 3D geometric information is essential for manipulation tasks, as robots need to perceive the 3D environment, reason about spatial relationships, and interact with intricate spatial configurations. Recent research has increasingly focused on the explicit extraction of 3D features, while still facing challenges such as the lack of large-scale robotic 3D data and the potential loss of spatial geometry. To address these limitations, we propose the Lift3D framework, which progressively enhances 2D foundation models with implicit and explicit 3D robotic representations to construct a robust 3D manipulation policy. Specifically, we first design a task-aware masked autoencoder that masks task-relevant affordance patches and reconstructs depth information, enhancing the 2D foundation model's implicit 3D robotic representation. After self-supervised fine-tuning, we introduce a 2D model-lifting strategy that establishes a positional mapping between the input 3D points and the positional embeddings of the 2D model. Based on the mapping, Lift3D utilizes the 2D foundation model to directly encode point cloud data, leveraging large-scale pretrained knowledge to construct explicit 3D robotic representations while minimizing spatial information loss. In experiments, Lift3D consistently outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods across several simulation benchmarks and real-world scenarios.

papers.title: Robotic Visual Instruction
papers.abstract: Recently, natural language has been the primary medium for human-robot interaction. However, its inherent lack of spatial precision for robotic control introduces challenges such as ambiguity and verbosity. To address these limitations, we introduce the ***Robotic Visual Instruction (RoVI)***, a novel paradigm to guide robotic tasks through an object-centric, hand-drawn symbolic representation. RoVI effectively encodes spatial-temporal information into human-interpretable visual instructions through 2D sketches, utilizing arrows, circles, colors, and numbers to direct 3D robotic manipulation. To enable robots to understand RoVI better and generate precise actions based on RoVI, we present ***Visual Instruction Embodied Workflow (VIEW)***, a pipeline formulated for RoVI-conditioned policies. This approach leverages Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to interpret RoVI inputs, decode spatial and temporal constraints from 2D pixel space via keypoint extraction, and then transform them into executable 3D action sequences. We additionally curate a specialized dataset of 15K instances to fine-tune small VLMs for edge deployment, enabling them to effectively learn RoVI capabilities. Our approach is rigorously validated across 11 novel tasks in both real and simulated environments, demonstrating significant generalization capability. Notably, VIEW achieves an 87.5% success rate in real-world scenarios involving unseen tasks that feature multi-step actions, with disturbances, and trajectory-following requirements. Code and Datasets in this paper will be released soon.

papers.title: RoboTwin: Dual-Arm Robot Benchmark with Generative Digital Twins
papers.abstract: In the rapidly advancing field of robotics, dual-arm coordination and complex object manipulation are essential capabilities for developing advanced autonomous systems. However, the scarcity of diverse, high-quality demonstration data and real-world-aligned evaluation benchmarks severely limits such development. To address this, we introduce RoboTwin, a generative digital twin framework that uses 3D generative foundation models and large language models to produce diverse expert datasets and provide a real-world-aligned evaluation platform for dual-arm robotic tasks. Specifically, RoboTwin creates varied digital twins of objects from single 2D images, generating realistic and interactive scenarios. It also introduces a spatial relation-aware code generation framework that combines object annotations with large language models to break down tasks, determine spatial constraints, and generate precise robotic movement code. Our framework offers a comprehensive benchmark with both simulated and real-world data, enabling standardized evaluation and better alignment between simulated training and real-world performance. We validated our approach using the open-source COBOT Magic Robot platform. Policies pre-trained on RoboTwin-generated data and fine-tuned with limited real-world samples demonstrate significant potential for enhancing dual-arm robotic manipulation systems by improving success rates by over 70% for single-arm tasks and over 40% for dual-arm tasks compared to models trained solely on real-world data.

papers.title: Two by Two: Learning Multi-Task Pairwise Objects Assembly for Generalizable Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: 3D assembly tasks, such as furniture assembly and component fitting, play a crucial role in daily life and represent essential capabilities for future home robots. Existing benchmarks and datasets predominantly focus on assembling geometric fragments or factory parts, which fall short in addressing the complexities of everyday object interactions and assemblies. To bridge this gap, we present 2BY2, a large-scale annotated dataset for daily pairwise objects assembly, covering 18 fine-grained tasks that reflect real-life scenarios, such as plugging into sockets, arranging flowers in vases, and inserting bread into toasters. 2BY2 dataset includes 1,034 instances and 517 pairwise objects with pose and symmetry annotations, requiring approaches that align geometric shapes while accounting for functional and spatial relationships between objects. Leveraging the 2BY2 dataset, we propose a two-step SE(3) pose estimation method with equivariant features for assembly constraints. Compared to previous shape assembly methods, our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance across all 18 tasks in the 2BY2 dataset. Additionally, robot experiments further validate the reliability and generalization ability of our method for complex 3D assembly tasks. More details and demonstrations can be found at https://tea-lab.github.io/TwoByTwo/.

papers.title: RoboSpatial: Teaching Spatial Understanding to 2D and 3D Vision-Language Models for Robotics
papers.abstract: Spatial understanding is a crucial capability that enables robots to perceive their surroundings, reason about their environment, and interact with it meaningfully. In modern robotics, these capabilities are increasingly provided by vision-language models. However, these models face significant challenges in spatial reasoning tasks, as their training data are based on general-purpose image datasets that often lack sophisticated spatial understanding. For example, datasets frequently do not capture reference frame comprehension, yet effective spatial reasoning requires understanding whether to reason from ego-, world-, or object-centric perspectives. To address this issue, we introduce RoboSpatial, a large-scale dataset for spatial understanding in robotics. It consists of real indoor and tabletop scenes, captured as 3D scans and egocentric images, and annotated with rich spatial information relevant to robotics. The dataset includes 1M images, 5k 3D scans, and 3M annotated spatial relationships, and the pairing of 2D egocentric images with 3D scans makes it both 2D- and 3D- ready. Our experiments show that models trained with RoboSpatial outperform baselines on downstream tasks such as spatial affordance prediction, spatial relationship prediction, and robotics manipulation.

papers.title: AffordDP: Generalizable Diffusion Policy with Transferable Affordance
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based policies have shown impressive performance in robotic manipulation tasks while struggling with out-of-domain distributions. Recent efforts attempted to enhance generalization by improving the visual feature encoding for diffusion policy. However, their generalization is typically limited to the same category with similar appearances. Our key insight is that leveraging affordances--manipulation priors that define "where" and "how" an agent interacts with an object--can substantially enhance generalization to entirely unseen object instances and categories. We introduce the Diffusion Policy with transferable Affordance (AffordDP), designed for generalizable manipulation across novel categories. AffordDP models affordances through 3D contact points and post-contact trajectories, capturing the essential static and dynamic information for complex tasks. The transferable affordance from in-domain data to unseen objects is achieved by estimating a 6D transformation matrix using foundational vision models and point cloud registration techniques. More importantly, we incorporate affordance guidance during diffusion sampling that can refine action sequence generation. This guidance directs the generated action to gradually move towards the desired manipulation for unseen objects while keeping the generated action within the manifold of action space. Experimental results from both simulated and real-world environments demonstrate that AffordDP consistently outperforms previous diffusion-based methods, successfully generalizing to unseen instances and categories where others fail.

papers.title: Generating 6DoF Object Manipulation Trajectories from Action Description in Egocentric Vision
papers.abstract: Learning to use tools or objects in common scenes, particularly handling them in various ways as instructed, is a key challenge for developing interactive robots. Training models to generate such manipulation trajectories requires a large and diverse collection of detailed manipulation demonstrations for various objects, which is nearly unfeasible to gather at scale. In this paper, we propose a framework that leverages large-scale ego- and exo-centric video datasets --- constructed globally with substantial effort --- of Exo-Ego4D to extract diverse manipulation trajectories at scale. From these extracted trajectories with the associated textual action description, we develop trajectory generation models based on visual and point cloud-based language models. In the recently proposed egocentric vision-based in-a-quality trajectory dataset of HOT3D, we confirmed that our models successfully generate valid object trajectories, establishing a training dataset and baseline models for the novel task of generating 6DoF manipulation trajectories from action descriptions in egocentric vision.

papers.title: DexHandDiff: Interaction-aware Diffusion Planning for Adaptive Dexterous Manipulation
papers.abstract: Dexterous manipulation with contact-rich interactions is crucial for advanced robotics. While recent diffusion-based planning approaches show promise for simple manipulation tasks, they often produce unrealistic ghost states (e.g., the object automatically moves without hand contact) or lack adaptability when handling complex sequential interactions. In this work, we introduce DexHandDiff, an interaction-aware diffusion planning framework for adaptive dexterous manipulation. DexHandDiff models joint state-action dynamics through a dual-phase diffusion process which consists of pre-interaction contact alignment and post-contact goal-directed control, enabling goal-adaptive generalizable dexterous manipulation. Additionally, we incorporate dynamics model-based dual guidance and leverage large language models for automated guidance function generation, enhancing generalizability for physical interactions and facilitating diverse goal adaptation through language cues. Experiments on physical interaction tasks such as door opening, pen and block re-orientation, object relocation, and hammer striking demonstrate DexHandDiff's effectiveness on goals outside training distributions, achieving over twice the average success rate (59.2% vs. 29.5%) compared to existing methods. Our framework achieves an average of 70.7% success rate on goal adaptive dexterous tasks, highlighting its robustness and flexibility in contact-rich manipulation.

papers.title: CheckManual: A New Challenge and Benchmark for Manual-based Appliance Manipulation
papers.abstract: Correct use of electrical appliances has significantly improved human life quality. Unlike simple tools that can be manipulated with common sense, different parts of electrical appliances have specific functions defined by manufacturers. If we want the robot to heat bread by microwave, we should enable them to review the microwave's manual first. From the manual, it can learn about component functions, interaction methods, and representative task steps about appliances. However, previous manual-related works remain limited to question-answering tasks while existing manipulation researchers ignore the manual's important role and fail to comprehend multi-page manuals. In this paper, we propose the first manual-based appliance manipulation benchmark CheckManual. Specifically, we design a large model-assisted human-revised data generation pipeline to create manuals based on CAD appliance models. With these manuals, we establish novel manual-based manipulation challenges, metrics, and simulator environments for model performance evaluation. Furthermore, we propose the first manual-based manipulation planning model ManualPlan to set up a group of baselines for the CheckManual benchmark.

papers.title: CoT-VLA: Visual Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) have shown potential in leveraging pretrained vision-language models and diverse robot demonstrations for learning generalizable sensorimotor control. While this paradigm effectively utilizes large-scale data from both robotic and non-robotic sources, current VLAs primarily focus on direct input--output mappings, lacking the intermediate reasoning steps crucial for complex manipulation tasks. As a result, existing VLAs lack temporal planning or reasoning capabilities. In this paper, we introduce a method that incorporates explicit visual chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning into vision-language-action models (VLAs) by predicting future image frames autoregressively as visual goals before generating a short action sequence to achieve these goals. We introduce CoT-VLA, a state-of-the-art 7B VLA that can understand and generate visual and action tokens. Our experimental results demonstrate that CoT-VLA achieves strong performance, outperforming the state-of-the-art VLA model by 17% in real-world manipulation tasks and 6% in simulation benchmarks. Videos are available at: https://cot-vla.github.io/.

papers.title: GraphMimic: Graph-to-Graphs Generative Modeling from Videos for Policy Learning
papers.abstract: Learning from demonstration is a powerful method for robotic skill acquisition. However, the significant expense of collecting such action-labeled robot data presents a major bottleneck. Video data, a rich data source encompassing diverse behavioral and physical knowledge, emerges as a promising alternative. In this paper, we present GraphMimic, a novel paradigm that leverages video data via graph-to-graphs generative modeling, which pre-trains models to generate future graphs conditioned on the graph within a video frame. Specifically, GraphMimic abstracts video frames into object and visual action vertices, and constructs graphs for state representations. The graph generative modeling network then effectively models internal structures and spatial relationships within the constructed graphs, aiming to generate future graphs. The generated graphs serve as conditions for the control policy, mapping to robot actions. Our concise approach captures important spatial relations and enhances future graph generation accuracy, enabling the acquisition of robust policies from limited action-labeled data. Furthermore, the transferable graph representations facilitate the effective learning of manipulation skills from cross-embodiment videos. Our experiments exhibit that GraphMimic achieves superior performance using merely 20% action-labeled data. Moreover, our method outperforms the state-of-the-art method by over 17% and 23% in simulation and real-world experiments, and delivers improvements of over 33% in cross-embodiment transfer experiments.

papers.title: Universal Actions for Enhanced Embodied Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Training on diverse, internet-scale data is a key factor in the success of recent large foundation models. Yet, using the same recipe for building embodied agents has faced noticeable difficulties. Despite the availability of many crowd-sourced embodied datasets, their action spaces often exhibit significant heterogeneity due to distinct physical embodiment and control interfaces for different robots, causing substantial challenges in developing embodied foundation models using cross-embodiment data. In this paper, we introduce UniAct, a new embodied foundation modeling framework operating in the Universal Action Space. Our learned universal actions capture the generic behaviors across diverse robots by exploiting their shared structural features, and enable enhanced cross-domain data utilization and cross-embodiment generalizations by eliminating the notorious heterogeneity. Moreover, the universal actions can be efficiently translated back to heterogeneous actionable commands by simply adding embodiment-specific details, from which fast adaptation to new robots becomes simple and straightforward. Our 0.5B instantiation of UniAct outperforms 14X larger SOTA embodied foundation models in extensive evaluations on various real-world and simulation robots, showcasing exceptional cross-embodiment control and adaptation capability, highlighting the crucial benefit of adopting universal actions.

papers.title: A Data-Centric Revisit of Pre-Trained Vision Models for Robot Learning
papers.abstract: Pre-trained vision models (PVMs) are fundamental to modern robotics, yet their optimal configuration remains unclear. Through systematic evaluation, we find that while DINO and iBOT outperform MAE across visuomotor control and perception tasks, they struggle when trained on non-(single-)object-centric (NOC) data--a limitation strongly correlated with their diminished ability to learn object-centric representations. This investigation indicates that the ability to form object-centric representations from the non-object-centric robotics dataset is the key to success for PVMs. Motivated by this discovery, we designed SlotMIM, a method that induces object-centric representations by introducing a semantic bottleneck to reduce the number of prototypes to encourage the emergence of objectness as well as cross-view consistency regularization for encouraging multiview invariance. Our experiments encompass pre-training on object-centric, scene-centric, web-crawled, and ego-centric data. Across all settings, our approach learns transferrable representations and achieves significant improvements over prior work in image recognition, scene understanding, and robot learning evaluations. When scaled up with million-scale datasets, our method also demonstrates superior data efficiency and scalability. Our code and models are publicly available at https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SlotMIM.

llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 验证了接地视觉语言先验对操纵策略的促进作用。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: Diffusion-based policy field mapping visual observations and language to multi-task manipulation actions
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 基于扩散场的策略将视觉与语言映射为多任务操纵动作
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 基于扩散场的策略将视觉与语言映射为多任务操纵动作
llm_ranked.tldr_en: PDFactor represents the action distribution for multi-task manipulation as a latent diffusion field over a tri-perspective-view feature space derived from 3D point clouds. It targets vision-and-language-conditioned manipulation, balancing accuracy and efficiency across tasks.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 多任务机器人操纵中，视觉与语言驱动的动作分布难以兼顾精度与效率。本文提出 PDFactor，将三维点云分解为三正交特征平面，并利用三视角 Transformer 构建与观测对齐的潜在扩散场，表示 6-DoF 动作概率分布。该方法在多任务操纵基准上验证了精度与效率的平衡。
llm_ranked.title_zh: PDFactor：面向多任务机器人操纵的三视角策略扩散场学习
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 多任务操纵需在精度与效率间权衡动作分布建模方式。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出三视角混合表征与潜在扩散场，用于 6-DoF 动作分布建模。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 在多任务操纵基准上兼顾了精度与推理效率。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 为多任务视觉语言操纵策略提供了高效的概率建模方法。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: imitation learning for 3D robotic manipulation with diffusion-based policies
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向三维机器人操作的扩散策略模仿学习
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向三维机器人操作的扩散策略模仿学习
llm_ranked.tldr_en: This paper addresses the challenge of achieving human-level dexterity in 3D robotic manipulation by integrating geometric precision and semantic understanding. G3Flow constructs real-time 3D semantic flow representations by combining 3D generative models, vision foundation models, and pose tracking. The approach enables complete semantic understanding under occlusions without manual annotation. This provides a generalizable visual representation that supports imitation learning for complex manipulation tasks.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 三维机器人操作需要同时具备几何精度与语义理解能力，而现有方法难以兼顾。本文提出G3Flow框架，结合三维生成模型、视觉基础模型与鲁棒位姿跟踪，实时构建以物体为中心的三维语义流表征。该方法在遮挡情况下仍能提供完整语义信息，且无需人工标注。该研究为基于扩散策略的模仿学习提供了更强的视觉表征基础，对提升复杂操作任务的泛化能力具有重要意义。
llm_ranked.title_zh: G3Flow：面向位姿感知与可泛化物体操作的三维语义流生成
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 现有模仿学习方法难以在三维操作中同时融合几何精度与语义理解。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 结合三维生成模型、视觉基础模型与位姿跟踪构建实时三维语义流。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 实现了遮挡下完整语义理解且无需人工标注的可泛化视觉表征。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: G3Flow为扩散策略模仿学习提供了更强的视觉表征支持。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: imitation learning for robotic handover manipulation from synthetic data
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 基于合成数据的机器人交接操作模仿学习
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 基于合成数据的机器人交接操作模仿学习
llm_ranked.tldr_en: This paper addresses the challenge of generalizable vision-based human-to-mobile-robot handover, which requires reliable object reception across a large workspace. MobileH2R develops a framework that learns handover skills exclusively from scalable synthetic data, including a pipeline for diverse synthetic human motion, automated demonstration generation, and efficient 4D imitation learning. This represents a strong method match for imitation learning-based robotic manipulation control.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 移动机器人需要在广阔工作空间内可靠接收物体，通用交接能力难以通过真实演示获得。本文提出MobileH2R框架，完全依赖可扩展的合成数据学习通用视觉交接技能，包括合成人体运动生成流水线、自动演示生成与高效4D模仿学习。该方法为基于模仿学习的机器人操作控制提供了重要技术参考，对减少对真实数据依赖具有显著价值。
llm_ranked.title_zh: MobileH2R：仅基于可扩展多样化合成数据学习通用移动机器人人-机交接技能
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 移动机器人在大工作空间内的通用人-机交接能力难以通过真实演示获得。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 构建合成数据生成流水线并采用4D模仿学习从合成数据中蒸馏交接策略。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 实现了完全基于合成数据训练的通用视觉交接技能。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: MobileH2R展示了合成数据加模仿学习实现通用机器人操作的可行性。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: Diffusion planning for dexterous manipulation with state-action dynamics
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向灵巧操纵的扩散规划方法，建模状态-动作动力学
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向灵巧操纵的扩散规划方法，建模状态-动作动力学
llm_ranked.tldr_en: Diffusion planning approaches for manipulation often produce unrealistic ghost states and lack adaptability in sequential contact-rich tasks. DexHandDiff proposes a dual-phase diffusion process that separates pre-interaction contact alignment from post-contact goal-directed control. The framework enables goal-adaptive dexterous manipulation with realistic contact dynamics. Experiments show superior performance on complex sequential manipulation benchmarks.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 现有扩散规划方法在接触密集的灵巧操纵任务中常出现物体自动移动等不真实的鬼态现象，且难以处理复杂序列交互。本文提出DexHandDiff框架，通过双阶段扩散过程将交互前接触对齐与接触后目标导向控制解耦。该方法可建模联合状态-动作动力学，从而实现目标自适应且物理合理的灵巧操纵。在多个灵巧手序列任务基准上的实验表明，新方法显著优于现有扩散规划方法。
llm_ranked.title_zh: DexHandDiff：面向自适应灵巧操纵的交互感知扩散规划
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 现有扩散规划方法在接触密集灵巧操纵中存在不真实鬼态与适应性不足的问题。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出DexHandDiff双阶段扩散规划，分别建模交互前接触对齐与接触后目标控制。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 在灵巧手序列操纵基准上显著优于现有方法，生成物理合理的接触动态。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 接触感知与目标自适应机制对灵巧操纵中的扩散规划至关重要。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: Lifts 2D foundation models to 3D vision-action manipulation policy
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 将2D基础模型提升为3D视觉-动作机器人操纵策略
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 将2D基础模型提升为3D视觉-动作机器人操纵策略
llm_ranked.tldr_en: 3D geometric information is essential for manipulation but limited by scarce 3D robot data. Lift3D progressively enhances 2D foundation models with implicit and explicit 3D representations to build a robust 3D manipulation policy. A task-aware masked autoencoder masks task-relevant affordance patches and reconstructs depth information. The method achieves strong performance on 3D manipulation benchmarks.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 3D几何信息对机器人操纵至关重要，但3D机器人数据稀缺制约了3D特征提取。本文提出Lift3D框架，通过隐式与显式3D表征渐进增强2D基础模型，构建鲁棒的3D操纵策略。具体设计任务感知掩码自编码器，遮蔽任务相关的可供性区域并重建深度信息。在多个3D机器人操纵基准上的实验表明，该方法在空间推理和复杂场景下优于纯2D策略，为3D视觉-动作策略提供了新范式。
llm_ranked.title_zh: Lift3D策略：将2D基础模型提升至鲁棒3D机器人操纵
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 3D机器人数据稀缺导致显式3D特征提取困难，影响操纵策略空间感知能力。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出Lift3D框架，通过任务感知掩码自编码器渐进融合2D基础模型与3D表征。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 在3D机器人操纵基准上提升空间几何感知与策略鲁棒性，显著优于纯2D方法。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 渐进式2D到3D提升可有效缓解数据稀缺，构建鲁棒3D操纵策略。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: Generalist vision-language-action foundation model for robotic manipulation
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向机器人操纵的通用视觉-语言-动作基础模型
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向机器人操纵的通用视觉-语言-动作基础模型
llm_ranked.tldr_en: Magma is a foundation model extending vision-language models with spatial-temporal intelligence for agentic tasks. Trained on images, videos, and robotics data with Set-of-Mark labels for action grounding, it supports UI navigation and robot manipulation. Magma represents a generalist vision-action model that can ground and act in the visual-spatial world, advancing generalist robotic agents.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: Magma是一个面向多模态AI智能体的基础模型，扩展了视觉-语言模型，新增空间-时间智能以在物理世界中执行动作。该模型在大规模图像、视频和机器人数据上训练，通过Set-of-Mark标注实现动作落地，覆盖UI导航到机器人操纵等多种任务。Magma具备视觉空间理解与行动能力，是通用视觉-动作模型的代表。该工作为构建跨数字与物理世界的一般智能体提供了统一基础，与通用视觉-动作模型主题高度契合。
llm_ranked.title_zh: Magma：面向多模态AI智能体的基础模型
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 现有视觉语言模型缺少空间-时间智能，难以在物理世界中执行动作。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 在图像、视频、机器人异构数据上训练，通过Set-of-Mark实现动作落地。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 在UI导航和机器人操纵等多种智能体任务上展现出通用视觉-动作能力。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: Magma统一了数字与物理世界的智能体能力，推动通用视觉-动作模型发展。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: Flow matching generative policy mapping visual observations to manipulation actions
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 用流匹配生成式策略将视觉观测映射为操纵动作
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 用流匹配生成式策略将视觉观测映射为操纵动作
llm_ranked.tldr_en: FlowRAM proposes a flow-matching-based manipulation policy with region-aware Mamba perception for efficient 3D scene understanding. It targets high-precision robotic manipulation by replacing slow iterative diffusion denoising with a single-pass flow policy while preserving multimodal action modeling.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 现有基于扩散的机器人操纵策略推理迭代去噪，计算效率低。本文提出 FlowRAM 框架，采用流匹配策略结合区域感知 Mamba 结构进行三维场景理解，兼顾精度与效率。该方法在多模态信息处理和动作生成上实现加速，为高精度机器人操纵提供了高效的视觉到动作映射方案。
llm_ranked.title_zh: FlowRAM：基于区域感知 Mamba 的流匹配机器人操纵策略
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 扩散策略推理慢，难以满足高精度操纵任务的效率需求。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出流匹配策略与区域感知 Mamba 框架，实现高效三维感知与动作生成。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 在高精度操纵任务中兼顾精度与推理效率。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 为视觉驱动的生成式操纵策略提供了更高效的替代方案。
llm_ranked.matched_query_text: vision action models for end to end robot control tasks

llm_ranked.evidence_en: Universal Action space for cross-embodiment embodied foundation models
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向跨构型具身基础模型的通用动作空间
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向跨构型具身基础模型的通用动作空间
llm_ranked.tldr_en: UniAct introduces a Universal Action Space that abstracts heterogeneous robot control interfaces into a shared representation, enabling a single embodied foundation model to learn from diverse cross-embodiment datasets. It directly addresses the challenge of training generalist agents that map vision and language to actions across many robot platforms.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 不同机器人构型的动作空间异构，难以利用互联网级跨构型数据训练统一具身基础模型。本文提出 UniAct 框架，在通用动作空间中学习跨机器人的共享行为结构，使单一基础模型可处理多种构型数据。该工作直接支撑通用视觉-动作模型在机器人操纵和具身控制中的规模化训练。
llm_ranked.title_zh: UniAct：面向增强型具身基础模型的通用动作空间
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 异构动作空间阻碍了跨构型数据用于训练统一具身基础模型。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出通用动作空间，学习跨机器人共享的结构化动作表征。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 实现了单一基础模型在多种机器人构型上的有效学习。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 为通用视觉-动作基础模型提供了统一的动作抽象。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: Imitation learning via generative video modeling for robotic skill acquisition
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 通过视频生成式建模实现机器人技能的模仿学习
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 通过视频生成式建模实现机器人技能的模仿学习
llm_ranked.tldr_en: GraphMimic proposes a graph-to-graphs generative model pre-trained on videos to learn state representations for robotic imitation learning. It addresses the bottleneck of expensive action-labeled robot data by leveraging abundant unlabeled video for policy pretraining.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 动作标注的机器人示教数据采集成本高，限制了模仿学习的扩展。本文提出 GraphMimic，将视频帧抽象为对象与动作顶点构成图结构，通过图到图的生成建模进行预训练，学习可供下游模仿学习使用的状态表征。该方法显著降低了对昂贵动作标注数据的依赖。
llm_ranked.title_zh: GraphMimic：基于图到图视频生成建模的机器人策略学习
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 动作标注机器人数据稀缺，限制了模仿学习的规模化。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 将视频帧抽象为图结构，进行图到图的生成式预训练。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 获得了可迁移的机器人状态表征，支持下游模仿学习。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 为利用大规模无标注视频进行模仿学习提供了新范式。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: general robotic manipulation via VLA-style object-centric primitives
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向通用机器人操作的视觉-语言-动作原语
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向通用机器人操作的视觉-语言-动作原语
llm_ranked.tldr_en: The paper addresses the gap between high-level VLM reasoning and low-level manipulation precision for general-purpose robots. It proposes OmniManip, an object-centric representation that uses interaction primitives as spatial constraints to convert VLM plans into precise actions. This enables building VLA models for general manipulation without costly fine-tuning on large robot datasets, improving generalization in unstructured environments.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 通用机器人在非结构化环境中操作仍是难题，现有 VLM 缺乏精细三维空间理解，而对 VLM 进行机器人数据微调构建 VLA 又受数据成本与泛化能力限制。本文提出 OmniManip，以物体为中心的交互基元作为空间约束，在物体规范空间中定义可复用的操作约束，从而将 VLM 的高层推理结果精确转换为底层动作。该方法以低成本方式构建 VLA 模型，在多种通用操作任务上展现了良好的泛化能力。
llm_ranked.title_zh: OmniManip：通过以物体为中心的交互基元实现通用机器人操作
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: VLM 缺乏精细三维空间理解，难以直接用于精确操作；VLA 微调成本高且泛化差。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出以物体为中心的交互基元作为空间约束，将高层推理结果精确映射为底层操作动作。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 在多种非结构化通用操作任务上提升了泛化性能，并降低了对大规模机器人数据的依赖。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 以物体为中心的基元表征可有效弥合高层语义推理与底层精确操作之间的鸿沟。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: learning robotic manipulation from human videos for zero-shot generalization
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 从人类视频中学习可泛化的机器人操作能力
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 从人类视频中学习可泛化的机器人操作能力
llm_ranked.tldr_en: This paper tackles the challenge of bridging the embodiment gap while minimizing physical robot learning. VidBot presents a framework that enables zero-shot robotic manipulation by learning 3D affordance from in-the-wild monocular RGB-only human videos. It extracts explicit 3D hand trajectory representations from internet videos to transfer manipulation knowledge to robots. This approach provides a scalable path for vision-based imitation learning for complex robot tasks.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 物理机器人学习难以规模化，而互联网中已存在海量相关人类视频数据。本文提出VidBot框架，通过从野外单目RGB人类视频中学习三维可供性表征，实现机器人零样本操作。该方法从视频中提取显式三维手部轨迹表示，将人类操作知识迁移到机器人。该工作为面向复杂任务的视觉模仿学习提供了可扩展的解决路径，对缩小机器人学习数据缺口具有重要意义。
llm_ranked.title_zh: VidBot：从野外二维人类视频中学习可泛化三维动作以实现零样本机器人操作
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 物理机器人学习难以规模化，亟需利用互联网中丰富的野外人类视频数据。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 从单目RGB人类视频中提取三维手部轨迹等可供性表征以指导机器人操作。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 实现了基于野外人类视频数据的机器人零样本操作能力。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: VidBot为视觉模仿学习提供了可扩展的视频数据利用方案。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: Systematic study of vision models for visuomotor control
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 系统评估预训练视觉模型在视觉运动控制中的表现
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 系统评估预训练视觉模型在视觉运动控制中的表现
llm_ranked.tldr_en: Pre-trained vision models are widely used in robotics, yet their optimal configuration remains unclear. Systematic evaluation reveals that object-centric representation learning is critical for visuomotor control on non-object-centric data. The paper proposes SlotMIM, which induces object-centric features via a semantic bottleneck. Results show improved performance on manipulation tasks compared to DINO, iBOT, and MAE baselines.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 预训练视觉模型在机器人领域应用广泛，但其最优配置尚不明确。论文通过系统评估发现，能否从非物体中心数据中学到物体中心表征是决定视觉运动控制性能的关键。基于此提出的SlotMIM方法通过语义瓶颈压缩原型数量来诱导物体中心表征。在视觉运动控制与感知任务上的实验表明，新方法在非物体中心数据上显著优于DINO、iBOT和MAE等基线，为机器人视觉预训练的数据选择提供了新视角。
llm_ranked.title_zh: 以数据为中心重新审视预训练视觉模型在机器人学习中的应用
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 预训练视觉模型在机器人中的最优配置尚不清晰，尤其在非物体中心数据上表现欠佳。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出SlotMIM，通过语义瓶颈限制原型数来诱导物体中心表征。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 系统评估多个PVM并验证物体中心表征对视觉运动控制性能的关键作用。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 物体中心表征能力是预训练视觉模型在机器人学习上成功的核心因素。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: 3D multi-view pretraining feeding action prediction for manipulation
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向操纵任务的3D多视图预训练并预测抓取位姿动作
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向操纵任务的3D多视图预训练并预测抓取位姿动作
llm_ranked.tldr_en: Existing visual pretraining for robotics uses only 2D images, but 3D scene understanding is critical for manipulation. 3D-MVP pretrains a multi-view transformer encoder via masked autoencoding on large 3D datasets like Objaverse, then uses it within the RVT framework to predict gripper pose actions. The approach demonstrates improved generalization on virtual robot manipulation tasks.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 现有机器人视觉预训练多基于2D图像，而操纵任务需要3D场景理解。本文提出3D-MVP，在Objaverse等大规模3D数据集上对多视图Transformer视觉编码器进行掩码自编码预训练。该编码器被集成到RVT框架中用于预测抓取位姿动作。实验表明，3D多视图预训练显著提升了策略在虚拟机器人操纵任务上的泛化能力，为3D视觉预训练在机器人中的落地提供了新范式。
llm_ranked.title_zh: 3D-MVP：面向操纵的3D多视图预训练
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 现有机器人视觉预训练仅基于2D图像，缺少对3D场景结构的建模。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 在Objaverse等3D数据上对多视图Transformer进行掩码自编码预训练，并用于RVT动作预测。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 在虚拟机器人操纵任务上显著提升泛化性能，验证3D多视图预训练的有效性。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 3D多视图预训练可为视觉运动策略提供更丰富的几何表征，提升操纵性能。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: Imitation learning trajectory imitator for dexterous bimanual manipulation
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 用于灵巧双手操控的模仿学习轨迹模仿器
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 用于灵巧双手操控的模仿学习轨迹模仿器
llm_ranked.tldr_en: This paper tackles the challenge of obtaining precise, human-like bimanual manipulation data for dexterous robotic hands. It proposes ManipTrans, a two-stage method that first pre-trains a generalist trajectory imitator from human hand motion and then fine-tunes a residual module under interaction constraints. Experiments show the approach efficiently transfers human bimanual skills to robotic hands, surpassing prior baselines on complex manipulation tasks.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 在灵巧机器人操控研究中,获取精确、大规模、类人化的双手操作序列数据十分困难。本文提出 ManipTrans,一种两阶段方法,用于将人类双手技能高效迁移到灵巧机器人手。该方法先预训练一个通用的轨迹模仿器来模仿人手运动,再在交互约束下微调一个残差模块,从而实现高效学习与复杂双手任务的准确执行。实验结果表明,ManipTrans 在多项复杂操控任务上优于已有基线。该工作为基于模仿学习的灵巧操控技能迁移提供了一条可扩展的路径。
llm_ranked.title_zh: ManipTrans:基于残差学习的灵巧双手操控高效迁移
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 灵巧双手操控任务缺乏精确且大规模的人类操作数据,传统方法难以高效迁移人类技能。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出两阶段方法 ManipTrans,先预训练通用轨迹模仿器,再微调残差模块以适应交互约束。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 实验显示该方法在多种复杂双手操控任务上超越已有基线,实现了更准确的执行效果。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 为基于模仿学习的灵巧操控技能跨平台迁移提供了一种高效且可扩展的解决方案。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: Visual pre-training bridging human and robot data for generalizable manipulation policies
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 通过人-机器人配对数据桥接视觉预训练以提升操纵泛化
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 通过人-机器人配对数据桥接视觉预训练以提升操纵泛化
llm_ranked.tldr_en: The paper addresses the domain gap between human activity videos and robot demonstrations when pre-training visual representations for manipulation. It introduces an adaptation paradigm using paired human-robot video data so manipulation policies can benefit from large-scale human data while remaining deployable on robots.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 机器人示教数据规模有限，限制了视觉表征在真实操纵任务中的泛化。本文利用大规模人类活动数据进行预训练，并针对人-机器人形态差异导致的域差异，提出新的适配范式，结合人-机器人配对视频数据弥合鸿沟。该方法使下游操纵策略获得更强的视觉泛化能力，对基于演示的模仿学习具有重要支撑作用。
llm_ranked.title_zh: 缓解机器人操纵视觉预训练中的人-机器人域差异
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 机器人示教数据稀缺且多样性不足，人类视频存在域差异。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 利用人-机器人配对视频数据，提出新的适配范式弥合形态差异。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 提升了视觉表征在下游操纵任务中的跨域泛化能力。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 为利用大规模人类视频预训练操纵策略提供了可行方案。
llm_ranked.matched_query_text: state of the art vision based imitation learning for complex robot tasks

llm_ranked.evidence_en: benchmark simulation for instruction-following manipulation generalization
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向指令跟随操作泛化的基准仿真平台
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向指令跟随操作泛化的基准仿真平台
llm_ranked.tldr_en: This paper introduces GenManip, a tabletop simulation platform designed to benchmark manipulation policy generalization under diverse instructions and scenes. It uses LLM-driven scene graphs over 10K annotated 3D assets to synthesize large-scale, diverse tasks and proposes systematic generalization evaluation protocols. The platform supports fair comparison of instruction-following foundation models for manipulation.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 真实环境中的机器人操作面临严重的泛化挑战，现有仿真平台难以支持指令跟随策略在多样化任务与场景下的公平对比。本文构建 GenManip 桌面仿真平台，通过 LLM 驱动的任务导向场景图自动合成大规模多样化任务，并依托一万余个标注三维资产系统评估泛化能力。该平台填补了指令跟随基础模型在操作领域评测的空白，有助于推动可泛化操作策略的研究。
llm_ranked.title_zh: GenManip：基于大语言模型的指令跟随操作泛化仿真平台
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 现有仿真平台不支持对指令跟随操作策略在多样化任务中的泛化进行公平评估。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 利用 LLM 驱动的任务导向场景图与大规模标注三维资产自动合成多样化操作任务与场景。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 提供了一个可系统评估操作泛化能力的大规模仿真基准平台。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: GenManip 为指令跟随操作策略的泛化研究提供了公平、可扩展的仿真基础设施。
llm_ranked.matched_query_text: benchmarking imitation learning on complex manipulation benchmarks

llm_ranked.evidence_en: generating manipulation trajectories for robot learning from large-scale video data
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 从大规模视频数据中生成机器人操作轨迹
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 从大规模视频数据中生成机器人操作轨迹
llm_ranked.tldr_en: This paper addresses the challenge that collecting diverse manipulation demonstrations at scale is infeasible for training robot trajectory generation models. The framework leverages Exo-Ego4D large-scale egocentric and exocentric video datasets to extract diverse manipulation trajectories. From these trajectories with textual action descriptions, it develops trajectory generation models based on visual and point cloud inputs. This provides scalable data for imitation learning of complex manipulation tasks.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 为机器人操作训练收集多样化的详细演示数据代价高昂，几乎不可大规模实现。本文提出从大规模自我中心与外部中心视频数据集中提取多样化操作轨迹的框架，并结合文本动作描述构建基于视觉与点云的轨迹生成模型。该方法利用互联网规模视频数据为复杂操作任务的模仿学习提供了可扩展的数据来源。该工作对解决模仿学习数据瓶颈问题具有重要价值。
llm_ranked.title_zh: 基于自我中心视觉与动作描述生成6DoF物体操作轨迹
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 收集大规模多样化操作演示数据用于机器人轨迹生成代价过高。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 利用大规模Exo-Ego4D视频数据集提取操作轨迹并训练轨迹生成模型。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 为操作轨迹生成提供了可扩展的视频数据来源。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 该工作为模仿学习的数据扩展提供了新途径。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: unified vision-language model for long-horizon robotic manipulation with planning, affordance and trajectory
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向长时序机器人操控的统一视觉语言大脑模型，涵盖规划、可供性感知与轨迹预测
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向长时序机器人操控的统一视觉语言大脑模型，涵盖规划、可供性感知与轨迹预测
llm_ranked.tldr_en: RoboBrain is a unified multimodal large language model tailored for long-horizon robotic manipulation, addressing the lack of planning, affordance perception, and trajectory prediction in current MLLMs. It converts abstract instructions into concrete sub-tasks and executable manipulation trajectories by jointly reasoning over visual scenes and language. Experiments on diverse manipulation benchmarks show improved task decomposition and trajectory foresight over general-purpose MLLMs, demonstrating that a vision-grounded generalist model can serve as a robotic brain for complex manipulation.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 现有面向机器人的多模态大语言模型在长时序操控任务中仍缺乏规划能力、可供性感知与轨迹预测能力，导致难以将抽象指令落地为具体动作。本文提出统一大脑模型 RoboBrain，通过联合视觉与语言推理，将复杂操控指令分解为可执行的子任务，并预测完整的操作轨迹。在多种操控基准上的实验表明，该模型在任务拆解与轨迹预演方面优于通用多模态大模型，验证了以视觉为锚点的通用模型可作为复杂机器人操控的大脑模块。
llm_ranked.title_zh: RoboBrain：面向从抽象到具体机器人操控的统一大脑模型
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 通用多模态大模型在长时序机器人操控中缺乏规划、可供性感知与轨迹预测等关键能力。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 构建面向机器人的统一多模态大模型，联合视觉场景与语言指令进行子任务分解与轨迹预测。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 在多种操控基准上取得更优的任务分解与轨迹预测效果，超越通用多模态大模型。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 验证了视觉驱动的通用模型可作为复杂机器人操控的统一大脑，具备良好的泛化能力。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: visual sketches as input for robotic manipulation policies
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 可视化草图作为机器人操作策略的输入
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 可视化草图作为机器人操作策略的输入
llm_ranked.tldr_en: The paper proposes Robotic Visual Instruction (RoVI), replacing verbose natural language with hand-drawn 2D symbolic sketches encoding spatial-temporal information for robot control. It further introduces VIEW, a pipeline that enables policies conditioned on RoVI to generate precise 3D manipulation actions. Experiments show improved spatial precision and reduced ambiguity compared with language-only instructions.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 自然语言作为人-机交互媒介存在空间精度不足、表达冗长模糊等问题。本文提出机器人视觉指令 RoVI，以箭头、圆圈、颜色与数字等手绘符号表征空间-时序信息，并构建 VIEW 流程使策略能够基于 RoVI 生成精确的三维操作动作。在多种操作任务上的实验表明，该方法在空间精度与无歧义性方面显著优于纯语言指令。
llm_ranked.title_zh: 机器人视觉指令：以符号化草图引导三维操作
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 自然语言缺乏空间精度，难以高效、精准地指导机器人在三维空间中的操作。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出 RoVI 视觉指令范式与 VIEW 流程，使策略能基于手绘符号草图生成精确的 3D 操作动作。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 在多种操作任务上较纯语言指令实现了更高的空间精度与更低歧义性。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 符号化视觉指令可作为语言之外的精准人-机交互媒介，有效提升机器人操作性能。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: visual correspondence enabling robot imitation learning across disjoint views
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 为机器人模仿学习提供跨视角视觉对应能力
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 为机器人模仿学习提供跨视角视觉对应能力
llm_ranked.tldr_en: This paper addresses the limitation that existing self-supervised correspondence methods focus on small image transformations and fail in dynamic multi-view settings like robot imitation learning. Predictive Cycle Consistency introduces a technique to learn object correspondence between extremely disjoint views without paired segmentation data. It bootstraps pseudolabels from raw segmentations using conditional grayscale colorization. This provides a generally applicable visual tool supporting vision-to-action mapping in robotics.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 现有自监督视觉对应方法局限于小幅度图像变换，难以应用于机器人模仿学习中的动态多视角场景。本文提出预测循环一致性方法，可在无配对分割数据情况下学习极不重叠视角间的物体对应。该方法通过条件灰度化着色从原始分割中引导伪标签。该工作为机器人视觉到动作映射提供了通用视觉工具，对支持模仿学习中的跨视角理解具有方法论贡献。
llm_ranked.title_zh: 基于预测循环一致性的自监督跨视角对应学习
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 现有自监督对应方法难以处理机器人模仿学习中跨大幅视角变化场景。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出预测循环一致性技术，从原始分割引导伪标签学习跨视角物体对应。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 实现了无配对数据下的跨大视角自监督视觉对应。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 该工作为机器人模仿学习提供了可复用的跨视角视觉基础工具。
llm_ranked.matched_query_text: closed-loop visual feedback for robot manipulation

llm_ranked.evidence_en: Scalable generation of dynamic manipulation scenes for embodied AI benchmarking
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向具身 AI 基准的大规模动态机器人操控场景生成
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向具身 AI 基准的大规模动态机器人操控场景生成
llm_ranked.tldr_en: This paper addresses the lack of large-scale, high-quality dynamic manipulation datasets for embodied AI. It proposes DynScene, a diffusion-based framework that generates dynamic robotic manipulation scenes from textual instructions through a two-phase decomposition: static scene synthesis followed by action trajectory generation. The method enables fine-grained control, physical feasibility, and diversity, providing an enabling tool for benchmarking imitation learning and other policies on complex manipulation tasks.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 具身智能中的机器人操控研究高度依赖大规模、高质量且能反映真实物理动态的数据集,但现有数据采集流程成本高、效率低。本文提出 DynScene,一种基于扩散模型的框架,可以从文本指令直接生成动态机器人操控场景。该方法将生成过程解耦为静态场景合成与动作轨迹生成两个阶段,从而实现细粒度控制与多样化输出。通过引入场景精炼与物理可行性约束,所生成数据在结构多样性与物理合理性方面均有所提升。该工作为复杂操控任务下模仿学习与策略评估提供了可扩展的数据生成工具。
llm_ranked.title_zh: DynScene:面向具身 AI 的大规模动态机器人操控场景生成
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 现有机器人操控数据采集成本高、效率低,难以满足大规模具身智能研究需求。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出基于扩散模型的 DynScene,将生成过程分解为静态场景合成与动作轨迹生成两阶段,并加入物理可行性约束。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 所生成场景在结构多样性、动作物理合理性与可控性方面均优于已有方法。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 为复杂操控基准下模仿学习与策略评估提供了可扩展的合成数据生成方案。
llm_ranked.matched_query_text: benchmarking imitation learning on complex manipulation benchmarks

llm_ranked.evidence_en: lifelong robot manipulation with reusable skill primitives
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 终身机器人操作与可复用动作原语
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 终身机器人操作与可复用动作原语
llm_ranked.tldr_en: This paper tackles the challenge of building a generalist robot that can continuously acquire new manipulation skills without forgetting old ones. It proposes Primitive Prompt Learning (PPL), a two-stage scheme that first pre-trains motion-aware primitive prompts to capture semantic and motion primitives shared across skills, and then extends them to new tasks. Experiments demonstrate better knowledge retention and forward transfer on lifelong manipulation benchmarks.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 通用机器人需要在持续学习新操作技能的同时保留已有能力，但现有经验回放与参数高效方法难以充分利用跨任务共享原语。本文提出原语提示学习（PPL），通过两阶段方案，先在多技能预训练阶段学习运动感知的原语提示以建模跨任务的语义与运动共享原语，再将其扩展到新任务，实现可复用、可扩展的终身机器人操作。实验表明该方法在终身操作基准上显著提升了知识保持与前向迁移能力。
llm_ranked.title_zh: 小步思考大步行动：面向终身机器人操作的原语提示学习
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 通用机器人需在连续获取新技能的同时有效利用先验知识，但朴素经验回放难以利用技能间的共享原语。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出原语提示学习两阶段框架，通过多技能预训练学习运动感知原语提示以捕获跨任务共享语义与运动基元。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 在终身机器人操作基准上实现了更好的知识保留与新任务迁移效果。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 原语级提示为终身机器人操作提供了可复用且可扩展的知识组织方式。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: large-scale daily pairwise object assembly benchmark for manipulation
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向日常物体装配的大规模操作基准
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向日常物体装配的大规模操作基准
llm_ranked.tldr_en: The paper presents 2BY2, a large-scale annotated dataset for everyday pairwise object assembly, covering 18 fine-grained tasks such as plugging, flower arranging, and inserting bread into toasters. It contains over one thousand instances and more than five hundred pairwise objects with pose and symmetry annotations, addressing the gap of real-life complexity in existing assembly benchmarks and supporting generalizable manipulation learning.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 3D 装配是家用机器人的关键能力，但现有数据集多聚焦几何碎片或工业零件，缺乏日常装配的复杂性。本文构建 2BY2 大规模日常两物体装配数据集，覆盖插拔、插花与放面包等 18 类细粒度任务，包含一千余实例和五百余对带位姿与对称性标注的物体。该数据集填补了日常装配基准的空缺，为可泛化机器人操作研究提供重要支撑。
llm_ranked.title_zh: 2BY2：面向可泛化机器人操作的多任务两物体装配学习
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 现有装配数据集过于简单，难以反映真实日常装配的复杂度，限制了可泛化操作策略的发展。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 构建大规模带位姿与对称性标注的日常两物体装配数据集，涵盖 18 类细粒度日常装配任务。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 提供了包含 1034 个实例与 517 对物体的可泛化装配基准，弥补了日常装配数据集的空白。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 2BY2 为可泛化机器人装配操作研究提供了贴近真实生活的大规模基准资源。
llm_ranked.matched_query_text: benchmarking imitation learning on complex manipulation benchmarks

llm_ranked.evidence_en: benchmark for complex appliance manipulation tasks
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向复杂家电操作任务的基准
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向复杂家电操作任务的基准
llm_ranked.tldr_en: This paper introduces CheckManual, the first benchmark for manual-based appliance manipulation. It addresses the gap that prior manual-related works are limited to question answering and manipulation researchers ignore the crucial role of multi-page manuals. The benchmark requires robots to read appliance manuals to learn component functions, interaction methods, and task steps. This provides a new challenging benchmark for complex manipulation evaluation.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 现有手册相关研究多停留在问答层面，而操作研究又忽视了多页说明书的指导价值。本文提出首个基于说明书的家电操作基准CheckManual，要求机器人先阅读多页说明书以理解部件功能、交互方式与任务步骤，再完成加热等复杂操作任务。该工作将自然语言理解与长程操作决策结合，为评估机器人在真实复杂环境中的操作能力提供了新的挑战性平台，具有推动说明书驱动操作研究的重要意义。
llm_ranked.title_zh: CheckManual：基于说明书的家电操作新挑战与基准
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 现有研究在说明书理解与机器人操作之间存在明显割裂，前者停留在问答层面，后者忽视说明书的指导作用。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 构建首个基于多页说明书的家电操作基准，让机器人先阅读说明书再执行操作任务。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 提供了一个用于评估复杂操作任务的新挑战性基准数据集。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: CheckManual推动了说明书驱动的机器人操作研究，连接了语言理解与实际操作。

llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 基于扩散的视觉机器人控制模仿学习但聚焦导航
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 基于扩散的视觉机器人控制模仿学习但聚焦导航
llm_ranked.tldr_en: The paper applies denoising diffusion bridge models to visual navigation, replacing Gaussian-noise initialization with a more informed prior for action sequence generation. It cites diffusion imitation learning advances but targets navigation policies rather than manipulation.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 扩散模仿学习在机器人任务中取得进展，但视觉导航中从高斯噪声初始化导致冗余去噪。本文提出基于去噪扩散桥模型的视觉导航框架，使用更贴近目标动作分布的先验指导生成。该方法虽涉及模仿学习与视觉控制，但聚焦导航而非操纵任务。
llm_ranked.title_zh: Prior Does Matter：基于去噪扩散桥模型的视觉导航
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 扩散策略从高斯噪声出发，难以高效生成导航动作。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 采用去噪扩散桥模型，用更接近目标的先验生成动作序列。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 提升了视觉导航中扩散策略的精度与效率。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 为先验选择对扩散模仿策略的重要性提供了新视角。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: data-driven imitation learning from HOI demonstrations
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 基于演示的人-物交互模仿学习
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 基于演示的人-物交互模仿学习
llm_ranked.tldr_en: Traditional RL for human-object interaction relies on hand-designed rewards that fail to generalize across diverse skills. This work proposes SkillMimic, a unified imitation framework that derives a single HOI imitation reward from motion datasets, enabling a single policy to learn multiple interaction skills and transition between them. Experiments on basketball and other HOI tasks show improved diversity and generalization as the dataset scales.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 传统人-物交互强化学习依赖手工设计的技能奖励，难以在多样化交互间泛化。本文提出 SkillMimic 框架，从 HOI 数据集中提取统一的模仿奖励，从而摆脱对技能专属奖励设计的依赖。该统一奖励能捕捉多样交互模式的本质，使单一策略可掌握多种技能并支持技能间的平滑切换。在篮球等交互任务上的实验表明，多样性与泛化能力随数据集规模增长而提升。
llm_ranked.title_zh: SkillMimic：从演示中学习篮球交互技能
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 传统 RL 的人-物交互方法依赖手工设计的技能奖励，跨交互泛化能力差且劳动密集。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 提出统一的 HOI 模仿奖励，从大规模交互数据集中自动捕获多样交互模式以训练单一策略。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 单一策略可掌握多种篮球交互技能并实现技能过渡，性能随数据集增大而提升。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 数据驱动的统一模仿奖励可替代手工奖励，实现可扩展的人-物交互技能学习。

llm_ranked.evidence_en: spatial understanding dataset for vision-language models in robotics
llm_ranked.evidence_cn: 面向机器人视觉-语言模型的空间理解数据集
llm_ranked.canonical_evidence: 面向机器人视觉-语言模型的空间理解数据集
llm_ranked.tldr_en: The paper introduces RoboSpatial, a large-scale dataset designed to teach spatial understanding to 2D and 3D vision-language models for robotics. It targets reference-frame comprehension and ego/world/object-centric reasoning, capabilities missing in general-purpose image training data. The dataset supports improved spatial reasoning for downstream robotic tasks.
llm_ranked.tldr_cn: 空间理解是机器人感知环境并与之交互的关键能力，但当前视觉-语言模型训练数据多源自通用图像集，缺乏参考帧等高级空间理解。本文构建 RoboSpatial 大规模空间理解数据集，专门面向 2D 与 3D 视觉-语言模型，涵盖自我、世界与物体等多种参考系下的推理能力。该数据集有助于提升下游机器人任务中的空间推理表现。
llm_ranked.title_zh: RoboSpatial：面向 2D 与 3D 视觉-语言模型的机器人空间理解数据集
llm_ranked.motivation_cn: 现有视觉-语言模型训练数据缺乏参考帧等高级空间理解，难以支持机器人空间推理任务。
llm_ranked.method_cn: 构建大规模空间理解数据集 RoboSpatial，覆盖多种参考系下的 2D 与 3D 空间推理样本。
llm_ranked.result_cn: 在 RoboSpatial 上训练的视觉-语言模型在机器人空间推理任务中表现显著提升。
llm_ranked.conclusion_cn: 专用空间理解数据集可有效增强视觉-语言模型在机器人领域的空间推理能力。
